title: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal
content:
A little over a month ago, Anthropic and AI infrastructure provider Nscale announced a $45 billion compute deal. Now the duo may be about to do it again.
Bloomberg reports that the two companies are said to be on the verge of announcing yet another $45 billion compute deal, citing people familiar with the matter. Those sources cautioned that talks are still underway and that the details could change.
If the deal goes through, it would be the latest in a long string of giant compute deals Anthropic has struck over the past year. TechCrunch reached out to Nscale and Anthropic for more information and will update this story if we hear back.
The massive amount of money being sunk into AI compute deals has spooked a certain segment of investors, who worry that companies are spending too much money for too little profit. Still, Anthropic has pressed on with such partnerships, driven by the belief that it will all pay off in the end.
Both Anthropic and Nscale are also currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year. Nscale is also seeking to go public, although Bloomberg reported on Monday that the company is experiencing investor pushback over its proposed valuation of $30 billion.

report.summary: Anthropic and Nscale are reportedly negotiating a second $45 billion compute deal, following a similar agreement announced about a month earlier.
report.background: The reported deal lands amid an AI infrastructure arms race. AI labs are racing to lock up massive GPU and data-center capacity for training and inference, and long-term compute contracts have become a strategic lever for both model quality and investor confidence. Anthropic has signed a string of giant compute deals over the past year, and Nscale has emerged as an AI infrastructure provider willing to build capacity at scale. The timing is notable because both companies are pursuing IPOs. Investors are increasingly questioning whether huge AI compute spending will translate into profits, and Bloomberg reported that Nscale is already facing pushback over its proposed $30 billion valuation. The earlier $45 billion Anthropic-Nscale deal was announced just over a month before this reported second agreement.
key_points: Bloomberg reports that Anthropic and Nscale are close to announcing another $45 billion compute deal. The people familiar with the matter cautioned that talks are still underway and terms could change, so the reported figure is not final.

The reported agreement would follow a $45 billion compute deal the two companies announced just over a month earlier. A second deal of the same size would significantly deepen Anthropic’s dependence on Nscale for AI infrastructure capacity.

The deal fits a broader pattern: Anthropic has struck a long string of giant compute partnerships over the past year. Securing large-scale compute has become central to its strategy for training and serving Claude models.

Both Anthropic and Nscale are pursuing IPOs. Nscale is reportedly facing investor pushback over its proposed $30 billion valuation, while some investors worry that massive AI compute spending is outpacing near-term profits.
report.impact: If the deal closes, it would reinforce a wider trend: frontier AI labs are locking up multiyear compute capacity through enormous private contracts, raising barriers to entry and making infrastructure partnerships a core competitive moat. For developers, more capacity could mean better availability and performance for Claude-based products and APIs, but it may also deepen dependence on a small set of infrastructure providers and influence pricing. For regular users, the payoff would likely appear as faster, more capable AI features, though the spending surge raises bubble concerns. A correction could force consolidation, change cloud pricing, or slow model releases across the industry.
report.tools: To follow the compute buildout, watch Nscale’s GPU cloud offerings and Anthropic’s Claude API pricing and status updates. For hands-on learning, SkyPilot helps orchestrate GPU workloads across clouds, vLLM provides open-source inference serving, and Kubernetes with Prometheus can track GPU utilization and cost. These tools help developers reason about capacity, deployment, and efficiency trade-offs without needing a $45 billion contract.
